conclusion: All six full circuits were rerouted fresh using the latest published stack at the start of this analysis. Neither routing mode completes a clean full board: 0/6 before and after. Phased routing retains 29/1,580 complete nets and 827 physical findings; fanout retains 22/1,580 complete nets and emits no signal traces. The selected fix removes a reproduced clearance violation during exact repair of earlier copper, with fewer vias, while preserving these board results.
controlsConclusion: All six original DDR controls pass all 310 nets before and after with zero physical findings and identical trace counts, via counts and wire lengths. Paired pipeline 9 / dataset 18 passes 16/16 before and after, with identical native PCB SVG hashes and 212.25 average vias. Its mean time changes by +0.31%; this is a single paired run and does not establish a speed improvement.
remainingBlockers: The full-board completion bottlenecks remain: dense BGA fanout cannot escape within the available boundary on iCE/Pi, i.MX6 and ButterStick, while other fanout runs exhaust their budget. In phased routing, ButterStick exhausts port-point pathing iterations; H616 fails the DDR bus solver's surface-approach geometry/matching check; OrangeCrab, Glider, i.MX6 and iCE/Pi exhaust the routing budget, with repeated joint DRC work prominent in captured timings. The broader plane-continuity correction reduced false findings but worsened Glider's actual copper, so it was rejected. The scoped reference guard addresses a demonstrated physical correctness issue; it is not a full-board completion improvement.
limitations: A successful Actions job means evidence was collected, not that the full board routed successfully.
The archived candidate workflow's formatting check failed on test formatting. The final source changes only that formatting; separate final-source formatting and byte-equivalence checks pass.
Fresh plane-routing contexts are excluded from the reference guard until their external anchors can be validated with plane geometry.
Native partial pours can differ between timed-out fanout runs; H616's fanout SVG differs while its complete nets, zero signal traces and physical findings remain unchanged.
The existing SEPIC repro retains tscircuit 0.0.3186 on both sides to isolate the router change; the six complete-board runs use the latest frozen stack above.
